questions: At lead 0.08 m, does the oval still end off track, and at what progress and max_error compared with lead 0.07 m?
Does steering_oscillation rise on the slalom compared with lead 0.07 m? If it does, is the lead overshooting?
Does the signal stay monotonic across the 15 mm spacing at the larger errors seen near the limit, or do the outer sensors drop out?
Is the remaining failure limited by controller gain or base speed rather than sensing? If sensing is no longer the limit, which geometry lever should move next?
feedback_request.requested_changes_if_any: If lead 0.08 m overshoots on the slalom, suggest the best lead between 0.07 and 0.08 m. If the oval improves but the s-bend still fails at the same progress, state whether sensor spacing (narrower or wider) or wheel_radius should change next.

intent: Test whether pushing the sensor row to the maximum forward lead (y = 0.08 m) continues the gain seen from 0.05 m to 0.07 m. Only the lead changes from iteration 2, so the effect is isolated from drivetrain and sensor spacing. Expected result: max_error below 0.05 m on the oval and s-bend, higher progress on all three tracks, and no large rise in steering_oscillation on the slalom.
learning: Iteration 2 confirmed that sensor forward lead is the lever with measurable effect (score 52.3 to 60.4, driven by the oval). Body width and drivetrain changes gave little. The off-track floor of 0.06 m is fixed by the contract, so further gains must come from lower error and more progress before the limit is reached. This iteration tests whether the lead trend continues to the top of its allowed range.
rationale: Evidence from three iterations: every development run ends off track at 11-16% progress, with max_error at 0.06-0.07 m. The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4). Even at the widest allowed body (0.18 m) that gives 0.0575 m, so the 0.06 m floor binds. Body width cannot help, and the robot must keep its error below 0.06 m. Iteration 1 showed drivetrain changes (track 0.10 m, mass 0.6 kg) only move the score by 0.14, with mixed effects by track. Iteration 2 moved the sensor lead from 0.05 m to 0.07 m and raised the score by 8.1 (52.3 to 60.4). The oval gained most: progress rose from 0.112 to 0.168, rms_error fell from 0.029 to 0.019, and control_effort dropped from 1.35 to 0.88. Steering oscillation on the oval also fell. The slalom and s-bend were essentially unchanged, and they still failed. The lead is the only lever that has produced a measurable gain so far, and the trend is monotonic in the right direction. I therefore push the lead to the top of its allowed range, y = 0.08 m, and change nothing else. Track 0.10 m, mass 0.6 kg, wheel radius 0.03 m, body 0.18 x 0.12 m, and the 12 mm sensors at 15 mm spacing all stay fixed, so any change is attributable to the lead. Expected result: max_error on the oval and s-bend falls further, progress rises, and the slalom oscillation stays flat or rises only slightly. Risk: at 0.08 m the sensors may see the bend too early, so the signal lags less but the controller may overcorrect on tight slalom bends. If that happens, the next geometry step is to narrow the sensor spacing, not to move the lead back.
